raw_case_text:
The patient is a 51-year-old man who arrived at our facility complaining of fever, chills, myalgia, and generalized weakness that had begun 5 days before coming to the hospital. His fever was continuous, and he reported that his eyes have been yellow for the previous 3 days; he also complained of a headache in the frontal area. He is a fishery officer and works in the rice paddies as well. He reported severe vomiting 4 to 5 times per day and a decreased appetite and a change in urine color during the previous few days.
The patient had no significant familial history of any disease. Except for one capsule of Omeprazole (20 mg) each day for heartburn; he reported no other current medications and no history of drug abuse history. The patient's physical examination showed the following vital signs: blood pressure 120/80 mmHG, pulse of 80, respiratory rate of 18, and temperature of 38 C. 
His conjunctiva was congested. No neck stiffness was detected. On both arms multiple petechia and, purpura were observed, but there was no sign of ecchymosis. The heart beat was normal. No organomegaly was detected in an abdominal examination. The lower limbs had normal appearance and function. 
The laboratory data are shown in Table 1.
After a brain CT scan the radiologist reported "multiple hemorrhagic lesions in the temporal and parietal lobes, especially in the left side" (see Figure 1).
The patient's chest X-ray was normal, and he tested negative for HBs Ag and HBs AB.
His diagnosis was reviewed, and in view of the deranged hepatorenal functions and seasonal prevalence (recent floods in the area where the patient resided), leptospirosis was clinically suspected, which was further confirmed by the positive serum IgM-ELISA (IgG value of 100 and an IgM value of 20). Epidemics of leptospirosis in our region and unavailability of Microscopic agglutination test (MAT) made us to consider IgM-ELISA for confirmation of leptospirosis. 
In an abdominal sonography, 70 cc of fluid were found in Morison's pouch, and the liver exhibited hepatitis-like changes. An MRI showed intracranial hemorrhage, especially in the left lobe.
With intracranial hemorrhage care and Ceftriaxone (1 mg/day) and Dexamethasone (8 mg two times daily) for 1 week and 15 unit platelets, his condition improved. After 26 days of hospital care with a normal platelet count and normal renal function the patient was discharged from hospital.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 51-year-old man presented with a 5-day history of continuous fever, chills, myalgias, generalized weakness, frontal headache, and 3 days of jaundice.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Symptoms began 5 days prior to admission with continuous fever, chills, generalized myalgias, and profound weakness. Frontal headache and yellow discoloration of the sclerae developed 3 days before presentation. He also experienced frequent vomiting (4 to 5 times per day), decreased appetite, and dark discoloration of his urine over the preceding few days.
subjective.past_medical_history: No significant family history of disease. Denied history of substance abuse. Home medications: omeprazole 20 mg orally once daily for heartburn. Occupation and epidemiological exposure: fishery officer working in rice paddies in an area with recent flooding.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for frontal headache, jaundice, dark urine, anorexia, severe vomiting (4-5 episodes/day), chills, and generalized myalgias. Denied neck stiffness, chest pain, or focal limb weakness.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature: 38 °C; blood pressure: 120/80 mmHg; pulse: 80 beats/min; respiratory rate: 18 breaths/min. HEENT: conjunctival congestion, scleral icterus, no nuchal rigidity. Cardiovascular: normal heart sounds, regular rhythm. Abdomen: soft, non-tender, no organomegaly. Extremities: multiple petechiae and purpura on both arms without ecchymosis; lower limbs normal in appearance and function.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission laboratory evaluation revealed deranged hepatorenal functions and thrombocytopenia, both of which normalized prior to discharge (normal platelet count and normal renal function). Chest X-ray was normal. Serology: negative for HBsAg and HBsAb. Abdominal ultrasound: 70 cc of fluid in Morison's pouch and hepatitis-like parenchymal changes in the liver.
objective.advanced_workup: Brain CT: multiple hemorrhagic lesions in the temporal and parietal lobes, prominent on the left side. Brain MRI: confirmed intracranial hemorrhage, especially in the left temporal/parietal lobe.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Severe leptospirosis complicated by multifocal intracranial hemorrhage (temporal and parietal lobes), acute hepatorenal impairment, and severe thrombocytopenia. Diagnosis was confirmed by positive serum IgM-ELISA (IgG: 100, IgM: 20) in the setting of regional epidemic prevalence. Acute hepatitis B was ruled out. Treatment & Outcome: Managed with intracranial hemorrhage protocol, 15 units of platelet transfusion, intravenous ceftriaxone (reported as 1 mg/day) and intravenous dexamethasone (8 mg twice daily) for 1 week. After 26 days of inpatient hospitalization, his condition substantially improved with full normalization of platelet count and renal function, allowing successful discharge.
